items.snippet: SpaceX秘密IPO文件及AI巨头上市计划或将重新激活公开市场融资通道。
items.raw_snippet: SpaceX’s confidential [IPO filing](https://fortune.com/2026/04/02/can-elon-musk-take-spacex-ipo-to-infinity-and-beyond/?utm_source=search&utm_medium=suggested_search&utm_campaign=search_link_clicks) has Wall Street abuzz about a reopening for [high-growth tech debuts](https://fortune.com/2026/03/20/spacex-openai-anthropic-could-be-3-of-the-biggest-venture-backed-ipos-of-all-time/?utm_source=search&utm_medium=suggested_search&utm_campaign=search_link_clicks), with OpenAI and Anthropic also looming in the wings. Despite the hype, the IPO market that [awaits](https://fortune.com/2026/01/15/ipo-boom-stock-market-nvidia-blackrock-spacex-openai-investing/?utm_source=search&utm_medium=suggested_search&utm_campaign=search_link_clicks) them looks nothing like 2021’s stampede. New Crunchbase [data](https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/record-breaking-funding-ai-global-q1-2026/) shows investors poured about $300 billion into roughly 6,000 startups globally in the quarter, up more than 150% both quarter over quarter and year over year. The market [began to stabilize](https://www.ey.com/en_ie/newsroom/2026/01/global-ipo-market-stabilises-in-2025-while-2026-pipeline-signals-potential-ai-led-mega-wave) in 2025: Global IPOs totaled 1,293 deals raising about $171.8 billion, a 39% increase in proceeds year over year, and the pipeline for 2026 turned more optimistic as larger tech names like Chime and Klarna finally got out. - [**Xoople**](https://www.xoople.com/), a Madrid, Spain-based AI data infrastructure company, raised $130 million in Series B funding from **Nazca** **Capital**, **MCH**, **CDTI**, **Buenavista** **Equity** **Partners**, **Endeavor** **Catalyst**, and others. - [**Natter**](https://www.trynatter.com/), a New York City-based AI conversation intelligence platform, raised $23 million in funding.

items.snippet: Asymco探讨人工智能时代企业价值的精确衡量标准与新型估值方法论。
items.raw_snippet: This is the precise and complete measure of the firm’s value but we use the shortcut of Market Cap since In most cases the Preferred stock and minority interest are negligible and if cash equals debt then the result is EV =~ Market Cap. it’s easier to calculate anyways as the shares outstanding and share price are easily available. When dividing both Market Cap and Earnings by the number of shares it becomes the famous P/E ratio or Price per share / Earnings per share. I used EV/FCF years ago to value Apple because at a time when it held huge amounts of cash. Without worrying who is or isn’t in the “Magnificent 7” I compiled the largest 10 market capitalization companies and looked at their P/E and EV/FCF ratios. | **Company** | **Market Cap** | **P/E Ratio** | **EV/FCF** |. items.title: Navigating the Tech Terrain: Case Study Series | Alvarez & Marsal
items.snippet: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly Generative AI (GenAI), is reshaping h...
items.raw_snippet: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly Generative AI (GenAI), is reshaping how private equity (PE)-backed portfolio companies approach product development. By moving teams away from manual, sequential workflows and toward more automated, predictive, and efficient operating models, AI has the potential to improve performance across the software development life cycle (SDLC). Applied thoughtfully across the development lifecycle, it can help accelerate time to market, improve product quality, reduce operating costs, and support stronger exit outcomes. This case study explores how the pragmatic application of GenAI can unlock meaningful value across product management and the SDLC. Rather than focusing on code generation alone, the approach highlights how GenAI can improve knowledge sharing, enhance implementation, reduce defect resolution time, and help teams move from ideation to execution more effectively. #### **Learn how a PE-backed healthcare technology platform applied GenAI to improve product management and software development life cycle execution.**. #### **Explore the first case study in the** ***Navigating the Tech Terrain*** **series for another perspective on how GenAI can help technology organizations improve performance.**.

items.title: AI创始人青睐零经验Z世代，称其具备独特优势
items.snippet: AI公司创始人表示，尽管缺乏经验，Gen Z在AI原生思维方面具有不可替代优势。
items.raw_snippet: # This AI founder is hiring Gen Z with zero experience because they’re not stuck in ‘old ways of working’—even as other CEOs slash entry‑level roles. “There are some positions where you actually want people that do not have the prejudice or the old way of working,” Chen tells *Fortune*. In the past few years, there’s been an explosion of new tools, job functions, and ways of working thanks to AI. “When you come as someone who just sees the problem and finds the best way to solve it,” Chen says, “it’s sometimes better than someone who has been doing the same job for so long and may just try to redo what’s been working for them in the past.”. To be clear: Chen isn’t *only* hiring Gen Z. He adds, “I think there is actually an opportunity for younger people, if they are resourceful and can actually flag in some way that they’re better than others, and more determined to succeed than others.”.

items.title: Google CEO Pichai says 'AI shift' opens opportunities invest startups
items.snippet: # Google CEO Sundar Pichai says 'AI shift' opens opportunities to invest in star...
items.raw_snippet: # Google CEO Sundar Pichai says 'AI shift' opens opportunities to invest in startups. * Google CEO Sundar Pichai said, in a discussion posted on Tuesday, that his company has increased opportunities to invest in startups because of the AI boom. With Alphabet poised to earn potentially $100 billion or more from its 2015 bet on Elon Musk's SpaceX, Google CEO Sundar Pichai said the explosion of artificial intelligence has opened the door to more startup investments. "You know SpaceX, Anthropic and so on so, I think now with the AI shift, there are more opportunities on which we can deploy capital in a good way and so we are doing that," Pichai said, in a conversation with Stripe co-founder John Collison posted on Tuesday. Alphabet first invested in SpaceX in 2015, putting in $900 million at a valuation of about $12 billion. In total, Google's investment in Anthropic now exceeds $3 billion, and it reportedly owns a 14% stake in the company.
